title: Integer queue
when: Implement a template queue with linked nodes; test FIFO, reuse and an empty dequeue.
question: Implement a generic Queue<T> using linked nodes. Do not use STL containers or arrays. Use using namespace std;.
Each node stores an item and a next pointer. The queue stores pointers to its first and last nodes.
Provide a constructor, destructor, void enqueue(T item), T dequeue(), and bool isEmpty() const. dequeue() throws runtime_error when empty.
In main(), enqueue 10, 20 and 30. Dequeue and print two items. Enqueue 40. Dequeue and print all remaining items, then attempt another dequeue and catch the exception.
Expected order: 10, 20, 30, 40, followed by the error. Both end pointers must be nullptr after removing the last node.
parts: enqueue
Allocate a node, attach it after tail, then move tail. If empty, head also points to the new node.
dequeue
Save the value, advance head, clear tail if now empty, delete the old node, and return its value.
Destructor
Delete remaining nodes; disabled copying prevents accidental shared node ownership.
change: Change int and the sample values; preserve the empty and one-node cases. The front() method is an optional extra.
watch: The final removal must set tail to nullptr. A subsequent enqueue must work. Never dereference head before checking isEmpty().

title: Job classes
when: Abstract Job with PrintJob and BackupJob; call execute through base pointers.
question: Create an abstract class Job with a protected integer id initialized by its constructor, a pure virtual void execute() const, and a virtual destructor.
Derive PrintJob, which stores a filename. Its execute() prints the job ID and filename.
Derive BackupJob, which stores a folder name. Its execute() prints the job ID and folder name.
Use using namespace std;. Add main() to create one job of each kind and demonstrate calls through Job pointers.
parts: Job
Stores shared id; = 0 makes execute pure virtual, so Job cannot be instantiated.
Derived constructors
Job(jobId) initializes the base part. filename(file) and folder(folderName) initialize each derived class’s own data.
execute() const override
Matches the base signature and supplies type-specific behavior.
main()
The objects live on the stack. The Job pointers borrow their addresses; do not delete them.
change: Rename the base and derived classes, edit their fields and output, and keep constructor initialization consistent.
watch: Include const on both overrides. The protected id is accessible to derived methods. Use a virtual destructor for safe deletion through base pointers.
expected:
Print job 1: notes.pdf
Backup job 2: coursework
expectedOutput:
Print job 1: notes.pdf
Backup job 2: coursework

title: Job queue
when: Combine abstract Job, derived jobs and a linked Queue<Job*>. 30 minutes · 25 marks.
question: Suggested time: 30 minutes. Total: 25 marks.

Classes and inheritance (8 marks): create abstract Job with protected int id, a constructor, pure virtual void execute() const and a virtual destructor. Derive PrintJob (filename) and BackupJob (folder). Each execute() prints its ID and stored name.

Linked queue (12 marks): implement Queue<T> without STL containers. Include a constructor, destructor, enqueue(T), dequeue() and isEmpty() const. Throw runtime_error on an empty dequeue. Handle removing the final node.

Main (5 marks): create Queue<Job*>. Dynamically allocate and enqueue PrintJob(1, "notes.pdf"), BackupJob(2, "coursework"), and PrintJob(3, "report.pdf"). Dequeue, execute and delete each job. Attempt another dequeue and catch the exception.
Use using namespace std;. The queue deletes its nodes; main deletes the jobs. Expected processing order is 1, 2, 3, followed by an empty-queue message.
parts: Queue<Job*>
T is Job*. Different derived job types share this base-pointer interface.
FIFO
enqueue adds at tail, dequeue removes at head, preserving arrival order.
Virtual dispatch
job->execute() runs PrintJob or BackupJob behavior according to the actual object.
Ownership
dequeue deletes a node, not its pointed-to Job. main deletes the job after execution. A virtual Job destructor makes that deletion correct.
change: Change the derived job types, their fields and execute() bodies. Keep the linked queue implementation and the dequeue → execute → delete loop.
watch: Do not call delete on stack-allocated objects. This example drains the queue normally; if you add operations that can throw during processing, also design cleanup for unprocessed jobs.
expected:
Print job 1: notes.pdf
Backup job 2: coursework
Print job 3: report.pdf
Empty queue
